synopsis: MineSim is an open-source, peer-reviewed scenario-based simulation test system and benchmark for autonomous trucks in open-pit mines, published in Accident Analysis & Prevention in April 2025; the cited precedent is academic simulation work only [f464, f15805, f1728]. It incorporates scenarios from two real mines and represents unstructured roads, irregular intersections and heavy-truck response lag, addressing a coverage gap identified in urban simulators [f465, f466, f3983]. Across chapters, the booklet treats MineSim as evidence that mine-specific closed-loop scenario infrastructure is feasible now and useful for scenario and planning validation [f330, f845, f1100, f15810]. This does not establish validated sensor physics: sensor models in dust, snow and fog remain unsolved, and the broader scene, dynamics and sensor simulation category is rated Low to Medium in heavy-off-road maturity [f15808, f15810, f916]. MineSim also demonstrates structured scenario methodology alongside ISO 34502, although the latter is road-specific [f833].
